This movie is raw, does nothing to tell any sort of story other than the one right on the screen. It’s…

title: Submarine
review:
“If I’m too late, I’ll stay down there with them.”
What an absolute delight. Comedy turned action/drama in such a masterful way. The tense situation in the end where they’re counting the bullets to make sure they have enough so they don’t suffocate was just *chef’s kiss*. Capra continues to impress me. Maybe it’s my lack of experience in the silent film genre but he just never misses.

title: Enter the Void

Gaspar Noé is a visionary directing films that no one else could even hope to make. I highly recommend going into this movie if you’re looking for a movie that will unsettle you while you’re appreciating some dope visuals.

title: Orozco the Embalmer
review: This is the kind of documentary that lingers. It doesn’t explain or dramatize anything. It just shows what it looks like when death becomes part of the background. Orozco treats the bodies like routine, just a steady rhythm of work that feels hollow and heavy at the same time. The scenes that stay with me are outside his workspace. Kids running around in the same neighborhood where corpses are wheeled past and laid out. It’s not dramatized in any way, it’s just what life looks like there. It’s sad in a quiet way. I hope things are better now.

title: The Phoenician Scheme

title: Cannibal Holocaust
review:
Alright! I finally made it back to Cannibal Holocaust after watching all of the Italian cannibal films before it. And I have to say, it still has not gotten any better than Man From Deep River. And honestly, I think I like Cannibal Holocaust even less than the first time I watched it. I didn’t remember just how boring it was.
Yeah yeah, animal deaths, sure. The rape is a much harder watch for me. It’s absolutely brutal in this movie. On par with I Spit On Your Grave imo.
2/5 is where this movie will live I’m afraid.

title: Emanuelle and the Last Cannibals
review:
A bit about me - I hate sex scenes for the sake of sex scenes. Having said that, I skipped about half of the movie, because that’s what half of the movie was. I knew that going in, but still, man.
As for the cannibal parts (the reason I watched), there were some brutal shots in this film. It’s worth a watch for that, but essentially the first half of the movie was a wash.

title: Searching for Cannibal Holocaust
review:
I’m glad I watched this. I have always heard that the animals killed were then eaten by the crew and the natives, but figured that might just be a way to calm anger amongst viewers.
But having heard that the animals killed were in fact 1) eaten and 2) very much enjoyed by the natives, I don’t really have a problem with it anymore.
As to the documentary, it was honestly kind of all over the place. I wouldn’t say it was terrible but it lacked a clear goal.

title: Last Cannibal World
review:
I can see why this could be considered the start of the genre over Lenzi’s Sacrifice!. I would personally still say Sacrifice is where it truly started, but this is where the formula for the genre began.
As for the movie itself, it’s gritty, it’s nasty, it’s honestly a tough watch at times. I do think Deodato hadn’t entirely found his stride for cannibal films yet, but this has the checkboxes ticked for what makes a cannibal film a cannibal film.

title: Man from Deep River
review:
Very clearly influenced by Mondo films, and the film that soft kicked off the Italian cannibal boom. I plan on trying to watch all of these movies this year and this was a good start.
Much more romance than cannibal exploitation, and the animal deaths were pretty hard to watch. I understand that it was par for the course but oof.

title: Citizen Toxie: The Toxic Avenger IV
review:
Well, I’ve watched all four Toxic Avenger movies within a week. I can’t say I’m disappointed to have done so.
This one SCREAMED 2000’s toilet humor. And as someone who DID love that in the early 2000s, it is now 2025 and I’m a bit older now.
Good gore effects, interesting premise, but overall the toilet humor just got well in the way.
My ranking: 2 > 1 > 4 > 3

title: Her
review: One of the most realistic visions of the future I've ever seen on film. I was able to see myself in Theodore's shoes throughout the entire movie. In a not so different timeline of my life, I can see myself going through what Theodore goes through in this story. The entire time, Theodore's story is emotional, wholesome, and heartbreaking and I love the character growth he has while experiencing these emotions. His friends are highlights of this show, refusing to judge him for what he loves, which is a complete 180 from what you'd expect going into this film. Excellent movie.
